What Makes a Place Feel Like Home
parenting_questions: If you were in charge of naming this snowstorm, what would you call it — and what would its personality be like?
What's the secret to making really good pasta sauce? If you had to teach someone who'd never cooked before, what would you tell them first?
Shepherd's Pie has all these layers — potato, meat, vegetables all stacked up. If you made a 'layer pie' of your perfect day, what would each layer be?
Dad's working as the Incident Manager today, which means he helps fix problems when things go wrong. What do you think would be the hardest part of that job?
You had swim lessons tonight — what's one thing in the water that felt easier than it used to? Even a tiny thing counts.
If you could swim anywhere in the world — an ocean, a lake, a pool on top of a mountain — where would you pick, and who would you bring?
You did science potions camp today! What was the wildest thing you mixed together, and what happened when you did?

Udon noodles come from Japan, where they slurp their noodles really loudly because it means the food is delicious. If our family had a food tradition from another country, what would you want it to be?
It's a Dan-and-Elsie night! If you could plan the perfect evening for just the two of us — anything goes — what would it look like, hour by hour?
Berries and cream for dessert — if you could invent a brand-new dessert that doesn't exist yet, what would it be called and what would be in it?
You just came from YAT — if you had to perform one scene from your life this week as a little play, which moment would you pick?
Clams live in shells at the bottom of the ocean. If you could live inside any animal's home for a day — a bird's nest, a beaver dam, a beehive — which would you choose and why?
You're the host tonight! If you could give our pizza party a theme — like a restaurant name and a vibe — what would it be?
What's one thing about each of your friends that you think is really cool — something not everyone would notice about them?

Stroganoff is a dish people have been making for hundreds of years in Russia. If our family had one recipe we'd pass down for a hundred years, what should it be — and what story would we tell about why it's special?
There's snow outside and warm gratin inside — total opposites. If you could design the perfect cozy day from the moment you wake up to the moment you fall asleep, what would every hour look like?

We're making pasta from scratch tonight — the dough, the rolling, everything. What's something you've made completely from scratch that you're really proud of? It doesn't have to be food — it could be anything.

Stir fry cooks really fast — everything happens in just a few minutes over high heat. What's something important that you think people rush through too quickly? What would happen if everyone just slowed down?
It's the first really warm evening of the year — 73 degrees! What's something about spring that you're most excited about? And what's one thing about winter you'll actually miss?

Tonight's dinner is fish, and we know that's not your favorite. But here's a question: what's something you used to not like — a food, an activity, a song, even a person — that you've totally changed your mind about? What made you change?

This pork has been cooking since this morning — hours and hours of slow heat and patience. If you had to spend a whole day doing just one thing, but with someone you've never done it with before, what would you pick and who would you invite?
This pulled pork has been cooking low and slow all day, just quietly getting ready. What's something YOU've been working on slowly that you're almost ready to show people?
Tech week started today! What's one thing your director or a crew member did that most people in the audience will never know about?

This is our last dinner all three of us before Mom flies to Portland. If you could give Mom one thing to carry in her suitcase that would remind her of us — not clothes, something more like a feeling or a memory — what would you pack for her?
It's just you and me tonight, roommate. If we weren't parent and kid — if we were just two people sharing this apartment for the week — what three house rules would you want us to have?

In your play, you get to become someone else on stage. If you could step into the life of anyone you actually know — a friend, a teacher, someone at YAT — for just one day, who would you pick and what do you think you'd learn?

You picked tonight's dinner — chef's choice, mac and cheese. If you were in charge of planning our whole weekend, not just dinner but everything from wake-up to bedtime, what would the Dan-and-Elsie Saturday look like before the big show?
You just performed! Forget whether it went 'well' or 'badly' — tell me about one single moment on stage tonight. What were you feeling right then, in your body and in your head?
If our Sunday Gravy sauce could tell the story of its life — starting as plain tomatoes sitting in a can — what would be the most exciting chapter?

Mujadara is sometimes called 'the food of the poor' in the Middle East, but people say it's one of the most delicious dishes ever invented. If you had to make the most amazing meal using only three simple ingredients, what would you pick and what would you call it?

Today is St. Patrick's Day — a day when people celebrate being Irish even if they aren't! If our family invented our own holiday — Corbiani Day — what would the traditions be? What would people eat? What color would everyone wear?

At science camp today, you mixed ingredients to create something totally new. What's something in real life — not in a lab — where combining two different things makes something better than either one alone?

Tonight we took last night's corned beef and turned it into tacos — a total remix! If you could take any one thing you already know how to do and remix it into something completely new, what would you create?
We had a whole free day together today. If you could bottle up one moment from today — put it in a jar on your shelf to open again whenever you're having a rough day — which moment would you save?

This week our corned beef traveled from Ireland to Mexico to Korea! If you were a food ingredient that could travel the whole world, what country would you visit first and what dish would you become there?

We're grilling outside in March and it's 84 degrees — it feels like summer crashed the spring party! If you were a weather forecaster, but for feelings instead of weather, what would today's emotional forecast be for our family?

Rain makes everything look different outside — puddles, reflections, a gray sky that changes the color of everything. What's something in your life that looks one way on the outside but is actually something completely different when you really look at it?

Every Tuesday we make pasta together — it's our thing. If someone filmed us making Babo Pasta and watched it like a documentary, what would they learn about our family that they couldn't learn any other way?

We're having pancakes for dinner — that's breakfast pretending to be dinner! What's something else that's way better when you put it in the wrong place or at the wrong time — like recess in the morning, or pajamas at the grocery store?

You just performed on stage tonight — amazing! Here’s a fun one: if you could choreograph a dance that tells the story of your whole third quarter at school, what song would you pick and what would the big finale move be?

You had your own evening tonight with your theater friends, and we had ours. Here's the challenge: describe your evening in exactly three facts — like a news reporter. No opinions, no 'it was so fun.' Just three things that happened. Then we'll do the same for ours.

It was 84 degrees on Sunday and 46 today — almost forty degrees different in one week! What's the biggest change YOU went through this week, from the beginning to right now? It doesn't have to be temperature — it could be a feeling, an idea, or something you learned.

We saw all those cherry blossoms today — they only last about two weeks and then they're gone. If you could keep one moment from today and put it in a jar on your shelf forever, which moment would you pick?

So we looked at that house today. If you got to design your own room in a brand-new house — any color walls, any kind of furniture, anything on the ceiling — what would it look like? Walk us through it like you're giving us a tour.
You had swim lessons today. What's something in the water that felt really hard at first but is starting to feel a little easier? Is there anything like that outside the pool, too?

It's the middle of spring break and we have nowhere to be tomorrow. If the three of us had to create a brand-new family holiday — a holiday that only our family celebrates — what would it be called and what would the traditions be?

We're having breakfast for dinner! What other rules do you think would be fun to flip upside down for a day? Bedtime at noon? Parents go to school and kids go to work? What would your upside-down day look like?
We just flew to a whole new city! When you stepped off the plane and looked around, what was the first thing you noticed that was different from home? And what was the first thing that felt the same?
We've been exploring Cleveland all day. If you were writing a travel guide for other kids visiting this city, what would be your number-one must-do recommendation and your one 'skip it' warning?
Chicken Parmesan takes a few steps — you bread it, fry it, sauce it, cheese it, bake it. What's something you're working on right now that has a lot of steps, and which step are you on?

We're listening to Vulfpeck tonight — they're a band that started by making super short, silly songs in a basement. What's something you started small that turned into something bigger than you expected?
You had swim lessons today — when you're underwater, everything sounds different and looks wobbly. What's something in your regular life that looks totally different when you see it from a new angle?
Corned beef hash is basically leftovers turned into something new and delicious. What's something old or leftover in your life that you could remix into something cool?

Earth, Wind & Fire is playing — those are three huge forces of nature. If you could have the power of earth, wind, OR fire for one day, which would you pick and what's the first thing you'd do with it?
We're making pizza tonight and everyone gets to choose their toppings — so here's the big question: Sophia, Faran, Elsie — if your personality was a pizza topping, what topping would you be and why?
We did forest bathing this morning — just being quiet in the woods. What's one thing you noticed out there that you'd never notice if you were in a hurry?
This gravy has been cooking since this morning — some recipes take all day to be right. What's something in your life that's worth taking a long time for?
Daddy was at AI Busy workday all day learning about how computers think. If a computer could learn one thing about YOU so it could be a really good friend, what would you want it to learn first?

Babo Pasta is our family's favorite — it's only ours because we make it together. If you had to invent a new family-only recipe that nobody else in the world has, what would it be called and what would be in it?
Dumplings are like little secret packages — the good stuff is hidden inside. What's something about you that most people don't see at first, but it's one of the best parts of you?
Today you came to Daddy's work and saw what grown-ups do all day. What's something you saw that surprised you — good or weird or boring or cool?

There's a whole fish on the table tonight — head, tail, everything. A lot of kids would say 'ew!' What's something that looked scary or weird the first time you saw it, but then turned out to be cool or delicious?

Mama's in Grand Rapids and it's just us tonight — dad-and-daughter taco night. If you and I started our own restaurant, what would we call it, what would we serve, and what would be our secret family rule that no other restaurant has?

stoic_anchor_quotes: Men look for retreats for themselves, the country, the sea-shore, the hills; and you yourself, too, are peculiarly accustomed to feel the same want. Yet all this is very unlike a philosopher, when you may at any hour you please retreat into yourself.

Some things are hurrying into existence, and others are hurrying out of it; and of that which is coming into existence part is already extinguished. Motions and changes are continually renewing the world, just as the uninterrupted course of time is always renewing the infinite duration of ages.

Remember that you are an actor in a play, the character of which is determined by the Playwright: if He wishes the play to be short, it is short; if long, it is long; if He wishes you to play the part of a beggar, remember to act even this rôle adroitly; and so if your rôle be that of a cripple, an official, or a layman. For this is your business, to play admirably the rôle assigned you; but the selection of that rôle is Another's.

We were born to work together like feet, hands, and eyes, like the two rows of teeth, upper and lower. To obstruct each other is unnatural. To feel anger at someone, to turn your back on him: these are obstructions.
Always to define whatever it is we perceive — to trace its outline — so we can see what it really is: its substance. Stripped bare. As a whole. Unmodified.
If one does not know to which port one is sailing, no wind is favorable.

Some things are within our power, while others are not. Within our power are opinion, motivation, desire, aversion — in short, whatever is our own doing. Not within our power are our body, our property, our reputation, our office — whatever is not our own doing.
It is not the man who has too little, but the man who craves more, that is poor.

The Time Daddio Ate a Spoonful of Dirt
story_lessons: Sometimes the things we think we don't like can surprise us, but it's also perfectly okay to have your own preferences.
Sometimes the most important things aren't missing — they're just waiting for their moment to appear.
The world is held together by people nobody remembers to thank — janitors, power linemen, cooks, crossing guards — and noticing their work is the first step toward gratitude.
The world you once feared is the same world that holds you, and it is full of magic if you are brave enough to see it.
The bravest thing you can do isn't always the biggest or scariest — sometimes it's just saying 'hi' to someone you don't know.
Love and stories leave traces in the places where they are shared — and if you listen closely, you can still hear them.
Big decisions take time, and that's okay — home isn't the building, it's the people you share it with.
Today's most embarrassing moment is tomorrow's funniest family story. Give it time. And also — don't eat dirt.
